annotations.text:
bmpl web redesign — verdict-first, Direction A (retained).
Keeps the current Primer-dark vocabulary: cards, 6-10px radii, system-ui, green/yellow/red verdict badges.
All numbers are sample data shaped like a real lookup (Muleyoxo, Holy Priest, +21). Confidence is per axis (dot next to each label), never global.
Radar: 6 axes on one 0-100 scale, rings at 25/50/75/100. A null axis (Consistency under 5 runs with signals) is a hollow point at the center, labelled n/a — never drawn as 0.
Direction B — denser monospace 'command deck'. Shown for contrast during the review; Direction A was chosen. Kept here for reference only.

Key selector: a global 'Your key' stepper (− +18 + · auto) in the header, remembered between sessions, applied to every new lookup. If the active tab was evaluated for another level, the hero shows a yellow hint 'Your key is +18 — re-evaluate for +18' that replaces the tab (cached data, ~0 pts). Level chip removed from the search box; spec chip stays.

Many profiles: compact chips (name · +level, class colour), × on hover, select circle for compare. Pick A (wrap) or B (scroll).

Sub-project 4 — on-demand deep-dive of a run's personal defensives (~3 WCL pts per run, cached forever).

Per run: Analyze · ~3 pts → Analyzed ✓ (expands the panel). Section header: Analyze all shown (~N pts).

Panel: Usage (casts / possible, %, bar; 'talent?' when casts are seen closer than the table cooldown) · Deaths (time, verdict, top killing hits, what was active / available / on cooldown; wipe deaths dimmed and not counted) · Audit (self-buffs not in the table with + major / + immunity / + minor / Ignore; the table used with Edit cd / Remove). Every correction is saved to defensives.json and re-applied at 0 pts.

Survival axis gets an 'N runs analyzed' chip once deep-dive evidence exists.

Today the axis descriptions exist but hide behind a native title tooltip and the row expand — nobody sees them.

A · ⓘ icon + popover: always visible, one hover away, keeps rows compact. Best when the user knows to look for an icon.
B · callout in the expanded row: explanation and evidence read together; the chevron makes the expand affordance obvious. Nothing new to discover, one click.
C · legend under the radar: the whole model at a glance (colours, weights, one line each), collapsible and remembered. Best for first-time readers; can be combined with A or B.

Recommendation: B + C (rows explain themselves when opened; the legend teaches the model once).

Issue #7 — hosted mode front. Local mode stays pixel-identical; everything here only renders when /api/status says hosted.

Pick one letter per artboard (A/B/C — 'B + C' combos welcome):
· Sign-in screen (401) and the notice treatment for ?denied=1 (1/2/3).
· Header: Re-configure / Quit / clipboard watch are gone; user menu with avatar, name, quota, Admin (admins only), Sign out. Quota label refreshes after each lookup / analyze and from 429 bodies.
· Deep-dive panel: 'Propose …' wording for members, pending / shared / rejected marks.

All colours are tokens.css values (yellow = pending, link blue = shared, red = rejected/quota). Sample user Muleyoxo, admin, 212 of 300 pts left.

Issue #8 — admin page at /admin (the menu's Admin item). Same sections in A / B / C, pick the layout:
· A tabs — one concern per tab, counts in the tab labels.
· B one page — everything visible, anchor sub-nav; longest.
· C dashboard — two columns, compact rows (24 h totals and Discord ids hidden), instance strip below.

Shared details on the 4th artboard: member 403 screen, proposal card (current → proposed diff, author, note to the author, Approve / Reject), empty queue, post-decision line, the two confirmations (role change, revoke sessions).

Not in this issue: the WCL error list (needs the audit log, #9) — the budget gauge ships without it; 'last backup' reads the file #10's deploy writes.

Issue #9 — hardening. The only visible change: the audit log on the admin page (logins, admin actions, quota refusals, security rejections, WCL errors). Same data in A / B / C, pick the treatment:
· A audit table — one section at the bottom, WCL errors are rows, the red chip filters them.
· B errors next to the gauge — the budget card gets a 'Last WCL errors' column (the issue's wording), the table below has everything else.
· C activity timeline — sentences grouped by day, same filters.

All three: a sixth 'Audit' anchor in the sub-nav with the 24 h error count. Rate limits and Origin rejections show as the usual error toast — no new UI.

Issue #11 — phase 2 (settings, privacy, account deletion). Pick a settings-page layout: A full page at /settings (consistent with /admin), B one compact card, C inside the user menu. Details board: verified WCL client state, typed-word delete confirmation, /privacy page, sign-in wording for open signup and the guild-denied notice, admin Ban/Unban.

Help page (spec 2026-09-19-documentation-and-help-design). Pick a layout: A sidebar TOC + long page, B admin-style anchor nav + accordions, C two-pane reference. Details board: the '?' affordance (a glyph, b 'how?' text, c evidence text as link), verdict hero, header Help link (local + hosted), user menu item, key-level scaling section. Numbers come from the effective evaluation config.

Region per lookup, remembered per user (setting like Your key). Pick A segmented control / B chip in the search field / C prefix of the search field. Below: the spec picker fed by the loaded character's specs (with run counts), free text before any lookup; tabs show the region only when it is not the instance default.

Guide for members who hit the shared quota: a /help card explaining why and how to create their own Warcraft Logs client (A one column with two step lists / B two columns with a checklist), plus the three places that link to it: the quota toast, the user menu's quota line, the Settings card hint.

French locale: where the EN / FR switch lives (A in the user menu / local header, B a chip inside the search field next to the region) and what the page reads like in French — player franglais, second person singular.

Personal page (self-review spec, decision 8): the member's characters, up to 5, added by hand until Battle.net linking (its own spec). Pick a layout: A list of cards / B table / C main first. All three show the season state, the five pillars of the last 4 weeks, Open (from history at 0 pts, else a lookup with its cost) and Sync (own WCL client when hosted). Details board: empty and full states, inline remove confirmation, local mode, the header link, the user-menu item and the home-page card for the main character, which never starts a lookup by itself.

Self-review phase 2 (spec 2026-10-10-self-review-control-design.md).
Top: a character outside My characters opens the result page exactly as before phase 1, plus “This is me” (pick A or B).
Below: crowd control in the owner's view. Run detail: pick A (one line per spell) or B (rate first, grouped by category). Dungeon panel, Control pillar states and the sync card are shared. Sample data: a Frost death knight, Den of Nalorakk +19 (captured run: Gnaw 8, Death Grip 5, Blinding Sleet 1 on 5 enemies); the spec median 3.9 is a placeholder until the reference is collected.
